topical prostaglandins do not appear to affect SLT outcomes.
the IOP-lowering efficacy of SLT was similar between eyes that did and did not receive topical prostaglandins, and that pre-operative IOP predicted SLT success.

the effects of topical prostaglanin analogues on SLT efficacy.
the effect of the topical use of prostaglandin (PGA) analogues on the IOP-lowering efficacy of selective laser trabeuloplasty (SALT).
the effect of prostaglandin use on the efficacy and success rates of SLT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLT is an effective and safe treatment for glaucoma and that the IOP lowering efficacy is not affected by the use of prostaglandin eye drops.
the use of prostaglandin in the treatment of glaucoma does not affect the efficacy of selective-laser trabeculoplasties.
the use of prostaglandin in combination with SLT is not contraindicated and does not affect outcomes of the procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IOP lowering efficacy is not influenced by pre-operative topical prostaglandins.
the use of prostaglandin in the preoperative setting did not affect the efficacy of SLT.
topical prostaglandins are not a contraindication for SLT and can be continued during SLT treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of topical glaucoma medications before and after SLTs does not influence SLT efficacy.
the use of prostaglandin analgesic drops before or after SLT does not affect the efficacy of SLT.
SLT is a safe and effective treatment for patients with glaucoma, including those who use prostaglandin eye drops.
